title: Vertical and horizontal scale in analytical databases

videos.script: Ana's warehouse fits on one machine with room to spare. Most do, for longer than people expect. {{fits}} But a shop that grows, or a business that keeps every click instead of every sale, reaches a point where one machine is not enough. {{grows}} There are two ways out. Buy a bigger machine: more cores, more memory, faster disks. Or buy more machines, and split the data between them. {{two}} The first is simple and has a ceiling. Ana measures it: four cores answer three times faster than one, not four, and a query given too little memory stops. {{up}} The second has no obvious ceiling and a long list of new problems. Which rows go to which machine. What happens when one machine gets half the work. What a join costs when its two sides live in different places. {{out}} This lesson has one machine, and it says so. The four machines are a hash and a count, which is enough to see where the rows would go, and why the choice of key decides everything. {{honest}}
